records.region: New Mexico, United States; Carrizozo Malpais–Salt Creek–Alkali Flat–Lake Lucero closed-basin setting with unestablished connecting watercourses.
records.candidate_name_role: Mapped middle/lower river component only; not an established representative identity for the complete selected Carrizozo-Malpais / Salt Creek / Alkali Flat / Lake Lucero route.
records.material_pending_reason: Two substantive links remain unestablished: the northern valley/lava-margin route through the Carrizozo Malpais corridor into Salt Creek, and the selected continuation south of the Salt Creek / Big Salt Lake playa complex through the dune-fringed floor and Alkali Flat into Lake Lucero. A mapped closed-basin setting and historical axial drainage are not evidence of present through-going watercourse continuity.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Seven original USGSTopo views support the northern canyon setting, the Carrizozo Malpais margins, a substantial Salt Creek segment, the Big Salt Lake playa setting, Alkali Flat and the final Lake Lucero setting. They do not establish the selected current watercourse across the lava corridor or the southward playa-to-Alkali-Flat-to-Lake-Lucero transfer. The independent field study supplies positive evidence of an intervening dune obstruction, rather than merely an absent name. The complete selected route remains source-material pending.
records.completion_scope: Seven original USGSTopo views support the northern canyon setting, the Carrizozo Malpais margins, a substantial Salt Creek segment, the Big Salt Lake playa setting, Alkali Flat and the final Lake Lucero setting. They do not establish the selected current watercourse across the lava corridor or the southward playa-to-Alkali-Flat-to-Lake-Lucero transfer. The independent field study supplies positive evidence of an intervening dune obstruction, rather than merely an absent name. The complete selected route remains source-material pending.
records.supported_name_scope: Scoped river-component candidate; whole selected system remains pending.

component_scope_limits: Salt Creek is confined to its directly mapped middle/lower channel; it is not extended to the northern canyon approach, Carrizozo lava corridor, Alkali Flat or Lake Lucero.

Ramsdale Canyon, Coyote Canyon, White Oaks Draw, the Carrizozo Malpais, Big Salt Lake, Alkali Flat and Lake Lucero are separately identified geographic settings, not alternate names for one uniformly named river.

Nogal Creek, Cottonwood Creek, Three Rivers, local spring channels, and the Andrecito Creek approach remain separate lateral systems; their proximity does not establish missing junctions with the selected route.
No exact banks, exact source point, current formal registry status, whole-route hydronym, official length or continuous perennial flow is claimed.

records.region: Ceará, Brazil; selected Choró river corridor.
records.candidate_name_role: Representative identity of the connected selected system, based on its receiving middle/lower Choró river, Pacajus reservoir passage and Choró Atlantic outlet; not a uniform name for its Cangati/Campos headward components.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Seven original primary maps establish the whole selected corridor at ordinary component scale: the north-turning Cangati/Campos headward opening around Iguaçu and São Salvador, the eastward Cangati valley through Targinos and Barbada, its confluence with Choró south of Caio Prado, the northeastward Choró through Itans and Aracoiaba-area junctions, the Chorozinho approach and Pacajus reservoir passage, and the lower Choró reaching the Atlantic at Barra Nova. Rio Choró is supported only as the representative system identity.
records.completion_scope: Seven original primary maps establish the whole selected corridor at ordinary component scale: the north-turning Cangati/Campos headward opening around Iguaçu and São Salvador, the eastward Cangati valley through Targinos and Barbada, its confluence with Choró south of Caio Prado, the northeastward Choró through Itans and Aracoiaba-area junctions, the Chorozinho approach and Pacajus reservoir passage, and the lower Choró reaching the Atlantic at Barra Nova. Rio Choró is supported only as the representative system identity.

component_scope_limits: The headward selection is not uniformly named Choró. Canindé mapping prints Rio Cangati on the opening near Iguaçu and downstream around Piedade/Targinos, and Riacho dos Campos along the intervening São Salvador/Juá corridor. These local labels are not converted into whole-feature synonyms or exact name-transition vertices.

Itapiúna mapping distinguishes the west-arriving Cangati from the south-arriving Choró near Fazenda Boa Sorte, south of Caio Prado. Some overprinted cartographic labels overlap this junction area; the clear separate approaches and connected receiving corridor support system correspondence without fixing a legal naming boundary.

Pacajus is a separately named reservoir on the Choró corridor. The COGERH technical sheet identifies Rio Choro as the impounded river. The regional state map prints Açude São Pedro in this reservoir setting, but that label is not promoted to a verified universal alias for Pacajus.

Rio Castro, Rio Pesqueiro, Rio Aracoiaba, Riacho Lagamar, Riacho Arecó and the other lateral drainage remain distinct. The selected route does not follow the northern Arecó reservoir arm or the artificial Canal da Integração.
No official registry name, current hydrological condition, exact bank or shoreline/mouth vertex, uniform scalar hydronym, or official total length is established.

records.region: Southern Florida, United States; northern Big Cypress wetland approach and Miami Canal/River coastal corridor.
records.candidate_name_role: Source-supported downstream river-component candidate only; Miami Canal is a separately named connected canal. No representative identity for the whole selected western wetland–canal–river route is established.
records.material_pending_reason: Actual headward and long wetland/canal-connector correspondence remains unresolved. Wetland polygons, nearby names, regional drainage membership, generic sheet flow and the retained model connection do not establish the selected route.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Primary USGSTopo views establish the southeastward Miami Canal/C-6 corridor, its urban canal–river links, the lower Miami River and Biscayne Bay terminal setting. The selected western opening east of Immokalee, southward approach through northern Big Cypress, eastward wetland traverse and northeast transfer into Miami Canal lack a mapped or otherwise primary-source-established through-connection. NPS original hydrology cartography and prose establish a wetland/sheet-flow setting but do not close those gaps. The full selected route remains source-material pending.
records.completion_scope: Primary USGSTopo views establish the southeastward Miami Canal/C-6 corridor, its urban canal–river links, the lower Miami River and Biscayne Bay terminal setting. The selected western opening east of Immokalee, southward approach through northern Big Cypress, eastward wetland traverse and northeast transfer into Miami Canal lack a mapped or otherwise primary-source-established through-connection. NPS original hydrology cartography and prose establish a wetland/sheet-flow setting but do not close those gaps. The full selected route remains source-material pending.
records.supported_name_scope: Bounded observed component candidates; whole selected system still pending.

component_scope_limits: Miami River and Miami Canal are distinct source-supported downstream component names; neither is extended to the far-western opening or Big Cypress wetlands.
USGSTopo also distinguishes North Fork Miami River, South Fork Miami River, Tamiami Canal, lateral canals and Biscayne Bay. These are not uniformly renamed after the downstream candidate.

No whole-feature scalar name, Korean name, official source point, current formal registry status, exact bank alignment, precise mouth vertex, complete present-day flow direction, or official total length is claimed.

records.supported_name_scope: No river-name scope established. Contextual ice-cap, lake, glacier, land and fjord labels retain their own feature types.

completion_scope.scope_explanation: Completion concerns direct bounded geographic reading and the absence of an established representative river name. It does not assert that the selected model is a mapped surface-water channel or that neighboring lake/glacier features form a single hydraulic chain.

records.region: Western Peary Land, northern Greenland; Inland Ice, exposed-rock valley belt and Hans Tavsen Iskappe to inner Adolf Jensen Fjord.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: All selected terrain segments and the actual terminal region are readable in lawful retained original cartography, but the modeled route spans distinct glaciated and ice-free settings without a supported whole-route or representative river hydronym. Glacier, lake, land and fjord names cannot substitute for a river name.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected coordinates lie in western Peary Land and the adjacent continental-ice margin. The terminal-side place is the inner Adolf Jensen Fjord setting, not Odinfjord, Harebugt, Frederick E. Hyde Fjord, or the distant Wandel Hav coast. General regional labels in earlier task descriptions do not replace the original graticule.

component_scope_limits: No river-name scope established. Contextual ice-cap, lake, glacier, land and fjord labels retain their own feature types.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
